questions.question: Does the phrase “binary operation on $A$” by itself say that the operation is associative?
options: Yes. All binary operations are associative by definition.
No, because a binary operation never combines elements of the same set.
No. Associativity is an additional property that may or may not hold.
Yes, but only when $A$ has more than two elements.

questions.question: On $\mathbb{Z}$, define $a\star b=a-b$. Is $\star$ a binary operation on $\mathbb{Z}$?
options: Only if $a\ge b$ for every pair chosen.
Yes; $a-b$ is an integer whenever $a,b$ are.
No, because subtraction is not commutative.
No, because subtraction is not associative.

questions.question: On $\mathbb{N}$, define $a\star b=a-b$. Which pair already shows that this is not a binary operation on $\mathbb{N}$?
If $A$ has 4 elements, how many ordered input pairs are in $A\times A$ for a binary operation on $A$?
On $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$, which ordinary operation is a binary operation?
options: Subtraction.
Addition.
Multiplication.
Division by the second input only when the second input is zero.

questions.question: Let $A=\{a,b\}$. A proposed table contains the value $c$ in one cell, where $c\notin A$. What fails?
options: Associativity only.
The number of inputs.
Closure in $A$.
Commutativity only.

questions.question: For $2\times2$ real matrices, which operation is a binary operation on that set?
options: Multiplying a $2\times2$ matrix by a $2\times3$ matrix.
Taking the determinant.
Matrix multiplication.
Extracting the first column.

questions.question: Why can a partially defined rule fail to be a binary operation even if its outputs usually lie in $A$?
options: A binary operation must be undefined for at least one pair.
A binary operation must be defined for every ordered pair in $A\times A$.
A binary operation only needs to work for pairs with distinct entries.
A binary operation may have several outputs for one pair.

questions.question: On $\mathbb{Z}$ define $a\star b=a+b-1$. Which element is the identity for $\star$?
options: there is none

questions.question: On $\mathbb{R}$, define $a\star b=\sqrt{a-b}$. Why is this not a binary operation on $\mathbb{R}$?
options: Because the rule uses two inputs.
Because square roots can never be real.
Because $a-b$ is always positive.
For some inputs (e.g. $a=1,b=2$) it is not real.

questions.question: On the set of even integers, define $a\star b=a+b$. Which statement is correct?
options: It is a binary operation only when both inputs are positive.
It is not a binary operation because some sums are negative.
It is not a binary operation because the set has infinitely many elements.
It is a binary operation because the sum of two even integers is even.
